problems.quote: merchandise deficit narrowed ($240 bn → $230 bn)
problems.problem: FY23 merchandise deficit was ~$267.6 bn, not $240 bn; FY24 deficit was ~$240.2 bn, not $230 bn.
problems.correction: merchandise deficit narrowed ($268 bn → $240 bn)
problems.verifierReason: FY23 merchandise deficit was $267.6B (not $240B); FY24 was $240.2B (not $230B). Correction matches official data.

problems.quote: Government approval (defence 74%, telecom 100%, pharma brownfield 74%, multi-brand retail 51%, media 26%, insurance 74%)
problems.problem: These sectors have automatic routes up to the stated caps; they are not solely under government approval. Defence up to 74% automatic, telecom up to 49% automatic, pharma brownfield up to 74% automatic, insurance 74% automatic. Only multi-brand retail 51% and media 26% require government approval.
problems.correction: Government approval for multi-brand retail 51%, media 26%; other sectors have automatic routes up to caps (defence 74%, telecom 49%, pharma brownfield 74%, insurance 74%)
problems.verifierReason: Original misstates route: Defence/Pharma/Insurance 74% & Telecom 49% are automatic; only Multi-brand retail 51% & Media 26% need govt approval. Correction is accurate.

problems.quote: The “National Standards Body” (Bureau of Indian Standards, BIS) acts as the national mirror committee for ISO and the national contact point for Codex
problems.problem: BIS is not the national contact point for Codex; that role belongs to FSSAI
problems.correction: The “National Standards Body” (Bureau of Indian Standards, BIS) acts as the national mirror committee for ISO; the national contact point for Codex is the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
problems.verifierReason: BIS is ISO mirror body; FSSAI is Codex contact point per FSS Act 2006.

problems.quote: The “Mutual Recognition Agreement” (MRA) negotiations with the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) and the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA)
problems.problem: EFSA is a risk assessment body, not a regulatory authority for MRA; MRA negotiations are with the European Commission (EU)
problems.correction: The “Mutual Recognition Agreement” (MRA) negotiations with the European Commission and the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA)
problems.verifierReason: EFSA is risk assessor; EU Commission negotiates MRAs.

problems.quote: WPI for manufactured products surged 12% year‑on‑year in April 2022
problems.problem: The actual WPI manufacturing inflation in April 2022 was 10.85%, not 12%.
problems.correction: WPI for manufactured products surged 10.9% year‑on‑year in April 2022
problems.verifierReason: WPI manufacturing inflation April 2022 was 10.85%, not 12%; 10.9% rounded is accurate

problems.quote: while the five‑year breakeven stayed near 4.2%
problems.problem: India's inflation‑indexed bonds are primarily 10‑year; the market breakeven referenced is the 10‑year breakeven, not a 5‑year one.
problems.correction: while the 10‑year breakeven stayed near 4.2%
problems.verifierReason: India's inflation-indexed bonds are primarily 10-year; 5-year breakeven not standard market reference

problems.quote: its urban component, the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016
problems.problem: The Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016 are not an urban component of the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan; they are separate rules notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. The urban component is the Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban).
problems.correction: the Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban) and the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016
problems.verifierReason: SWM Rules 2016 are statutory rules under EPA 1986, not a mission component; SBM(Urban) is the urban mission component.

problems.quote: 30 % collection and recycling of rigid plastic packaging by 2025‑26
problems.problem: The Plastic Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2022 set a 30% recycling target for rigid plastic packaging for 2024‑25; the target for 2025‑26 is 40%.
problems.correction: 40 % collection and recycling of rigid plastic packaging by 2025‑26
problems.verifierReason: PWM Amendment Rules 2022 Schedule II sets 30% recycling for rigid plastic in 2024-25 and 40% in 2025-26.

problems.quote: a sharply negative convenience yield signals scarce physical stocks
problems.problem: A negative convenience yield indicates abundant stocks; a positive (high) convenience yield signals scarcity.
problems.correction: a sharply positive convenience yield signals scarce physical stocks
problems.verifierReason: Convenience yield theory: high positive = scarcity; negative = abundance.

problems.quote: The Bank of England’s 2013‑14 activation of the CCyB coincided with a moderation of house‑price inflation
problems.problem: The BoE did not activate the CCyB in 2013‑14; the framework was introduced then but the first activation was in 2016.
problems.correction: The Bank of England’s 2016 activation of the CCyB coincided with a moderation of house‑price inflation
problems.verifierReason: CCyB framework introduced 2013; first activation announced March 2016.

problems.quote: dynamic fuel pricing mechanism in 2017, which aligns retail prices with international benchmarks on a fortnightly basis
problems.problem: Dynamic fuel pricing introduced in 2017 revises prices daily, not fortnightly.
problems.correction: dynamic fuel pricing mechanism in 2017, which aligns retail prices with international benchmarks on a daily basis
problems.verifierReason: India switched to daily petrol/diesel price revision in June 2017.

problems.quote: a 125‑basis‑point repo hike between May and October 2013
problems.problem: The RBI hiked the repo rate by 75 basis points (three 25‑bps hikes) between May and October 2013, not 125 bps.
problems.correction: a 75‑basis‑point repo hike between May and October 2013
problems.verifierReason: RBI repo hikes: 3×25 bps in May, Jul, Sep 2013 = 75 bps.

problems.quote: The 2016‑17 Monetary Policy Framework Agreement mandates that the RBI “take into account” the exchange rate while setting the policy rate
problems.problem: The Monetary Policy Framework Agreement (2016) sets the inflation target and establishes the MPC; it does not mandate the RBI to take the exchange rate into account.
problems.correction: The 2016 Monetary Policy Framework Agreement sets the inflation target and does not require exchange‑rate consideration.
problems.verifierReason: MPFA 2016 sets inflation target & MPC; no exchange-rate mandate.

problems.quote: Sweden’s Riksbank experimented with a price‑level target in the 1990s but reverted to inflation targeting after the 2008 crisis
problems.problem: Sweden adopted inflation targeting in 1993 and never used a price‑level target in the 1990s.
problems.correction: Sweden’s Riksbank has used inflation targeting since 1993 and did not experiment with a price‑level target.
problems.verifierReason: Riksbank adopted inflation targeting in 1993; never used price-level target.

problems.quote: estimated at 12‑15 percent of retail sales in 2023
problems.problem: E‑commerce share of retail sales in India in 2023 was around 7‑8%, not 12‑15%.
problems.correction: estimated at about 7‑8 percent of retail sales in 2023
problems.verifierReason: India e-commerce share of retail sales in 2023 was ~7-8%, not 12-15%.

problems.quote: The FRBM Act mandates a fiscal deficit target of 3 % of GDP by 2025‑26
problems.problem: The FRBM Act (as amended in 2018) mandates a 3% fiscal deficit target by 2020‑21, not 2025‑26. The current glide path announced in Budget 2021‑22 targets 4.5% by 2025‑26.
problems.correction: The FRBM Act mandates a fiscal deficit target of 3% of GDP by 2020‑21; the current glide path targets 4.5% by 2025‑26.
problems.verifierReason: FRBM Act amended 2018 sets 3% target for 2020-21; Budget 2021-22 glide path targets 4.5% by 2025-26

problems.quote: The 15th Finance Commission recommended that the Centre and states publish a “deficit‑adjusted‑for‑nominal‑GDP‑growth” metric alongside the headline ratio
problems.problem: The 15th Finance Commission recommended a cyclically adjusted (structural) deficit measure, not a metric explicitly named “deficit‑adjusted‑for‑nominal‑GDP‑growth”.
problems.correction: The 15th Finance Commission recommended that the Centre and states publish a cyclically adjusted (structural) deficit metric alongside the headline ratio.
problems.verifierReason: 15th FC report (Ch.4, para 4.147-4.148) recommends 'cyclically adjusted deficit' not the quoted phrase

problems.quote: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (Amendment) Bill, 2023 proposes a statutory requirement for the Finance Minister to table a “Revenue Forecast Accuracy Statement” within three months of
problems.problem: No FRBM (Amendment) Bill was introduced in 2023; the FRBM Act was last amended in 2018.
problems.correction: No FRBM (Amendment) Bill was introduced in 2023; the last amendment was in 2018.
problems.verifierReason: No FRBM Amendment Bill introduced in 2023; last amendment was Finance Act 2018

problems.quote: periods when the fiscal deficit stayed within the FRBM corridor (e.g., 2010‑11 to 2013‑14)
problems.problem: The fiscal deficit in 2010‑11 and 2011‑12 exceeded the original FRBM target of 3% of GDP; the revised glide path under the 2012 amendment applied only from 2012‑13 onward.
problems.correction: periods when the fiscal deficit followed the revised FRBM glide path (e.g., 2012‑13 to 2013‑14)
problems.verifierReason: Original cites 2010‑11 to 2013‑14; FRBM revised glide path started 2012‑13, earlier years exceeded 3% target.

problems.quote: The RBI’s 2015‑16 macroprudential tightening — raising risk weights on high‑LTV housing loans
problems.problem: The risk‑weight increase for high‑LTV housing loans was announced in 2013 (and refined in 2014), not in 2015‑16.
problems.correction: The RBI’s 2013 macroprudential tightening — raising risk weights on high‑LTV housing loans
problems.verifierReason: Risk-weight hike for high-LTV housing loans announced in 2013, not 2015‑16.

problems.quote: a 4‑2 government‑central bank voting split
problems.problem: The MPC has three RBI members and three government‑appointed external members (3‑3), with the Governor having a casting vote; it is not a 4‑2 split.
problems.correction: a 3‑3 voting split between RBI and government‑appointed members
problems.verifierReason: MPC has 3 RBI + 3 government members (3‑3), not 4‑2.

problems.quote: RBI's 2022 'External Benchmark-Based Lending Rate' (EBLR) mandate
problems.problem: The EBLR mandate was introduced in 2019 (effective October 1, 2019), not 2022.
problems.correction: RBI's 2019 'External Benchmark-Based Lending Rate' (EBLR) mandate
problems.verifierReason: EBLR mandate effective Oct 1, 2019 per RBI circular, not 2022.

problems.quote: a 15 % rise in Brent crude (from $108 to $124 per barrel)
problems.problem: Brent crude did not reach $124 in 2013; it rose from ~$108 to ~$115.
problems.correction: a rise in Brent crude from about $108 to about $115 per barrel
problems.verifierReason: Brent crude peaked ~$115 in 2013; $124 reached in 2012, not 2013.

problems.quote: WPI inflation jumped from 4.7 % (April 2013) to 7.5 % (August 2013)
problems.problem: WPI inflation in August 2013 was 6.1%, not 7.5%.
problems.correction: WPI inflation rose from 4.7% (April 2013) to 6.1% (August 2013)
problems.verifierReason: Official WPI data shows Aug 2013 inflation at 6.1%, not 7.5%.

problems.quote: CPI inflation rose from 9.3 % to 10.7 % over the same period
problems.problem: CPI inflation in August 2013 was ~9.5%, not 10.7%.
problems.correction: CPI inflation rose from 9.3% to about 9.5%
problems.verifierReason: CPI combined inflation Aug 2013 was ~9.5%, not 10.7%.

problems.quote: combined (Centre + States) debt-to-GDP ratio stands near 90 %, well above the FRBM threshold
problems.problem: The FRBM threshold (40%) applies only to central government debt, not combined debt.
problems.correction: combined (Centre + States) debt-to-GDP ratio stands near 90 %, far above the FRBM's central-government target of 40%
problems.verifierReason: FRBM 40% target applies to Centre only; combined debt ~90% is correct.

problems.quote: Micro-level surveys (NSSO 78th round, 2020-21) show that Jan Dhan account holders increased per-capita consumption by 4-6 % within two years of account opening
problems.problem: NSSO 78th round is a cross-sectional survey and cannot measure consumption changes within two years of account opening.
problems.correction: Micro-level studies indicate that Jan Dhan account holders increased per-capita consumption by 4-6% within two years of account opening
problems.verifierReason: NSSO 78th round is cross-sectional; cannot measure within-two-years change.

problems.quote: Once headline CPI breached the upper tolerance band, the RBI discontinued GSAP and resumed conventional tightening
problems.problem: Incorrect timeline: CPI breached 6% in May 2021, but GSAP continued until September 2021 and policy rate hikes began only in May 2022.
problems.correction: The RBI continued GSAP until September 2021 and started rate hikes in May 2022.
problems.verifierReason: Original implies immediate GSAP stop and rate hikes on CPI breach; actually GSAP ran till Sep 2021, hikes began May 2022. Correction fixes timeline accurately.

problems.quote: contributing to a persistent disinflationary impulse that required aggressive monetary easing
problems.problem: Both the 2008‑09 crisis and the 2020‑21 pandemic were followed by rising inflation in India, not persistent disinflation; the 2020 easing responded to a growth shock.
problems.correction: but inflation rose after both episodes, and 2020 easing targeted growth, not disinflation.
problems.verifierReason: Post-2008 and post-2020 saw rising/sticky inflation, not persistent disinflation; 2020 easing explicitly targeted growth shock. Correction accurately reframes.
